values.title: Where our beans come from
values.excerpt: Six single-origin coffees sit on our bar. Here is how we choose them and who grows them.
values.image_alt: Green coffee beans in a roasting drum beside a burlap sack
values.author: The Ember team

children.text: Every coffee on our bar comes from a single farm or co-operative. We taste dozens of samples each season and keep only the ones we would happily drink all morning.
We pay above the market price and buy the same lots year after year, so the farms can plan and we can follow how each crop changes. The bag always names the farm and the harvest.

values.title: A morning at the roastery
values.excerpt: Roasting day starts before the doors open. Here is what happens between the green bag and the cup.
values.image_alt: Freshly roasted beans pouring into the cooling tray
values.author: The Ember team

children.text: Roasting days begin at six. The drum is warmed, the first batch is weighed and Maya listens for the first crack, the sound that tells her the beans are close.
Each batch is cooled, tasted and logged before it is bagged. Anything that is not right goes back into the notes for next time, never onto the shelf.

values.title: Brewing a better pour-over at home
values.excerpt: Four small habits that make a pour-over taste cleaner and sweeter.
values.image_alt: Hot water poured from a gooseneck kettle over a pour-over dripper
values.author: The Ember team

children.text: Weigh the coffee and the water instead of guessing: sixty grams of coffee to a litre of water is a good place to start. Grind just before you brew, and rinse the paper filter so it does not leave a taste.
Pour in slow circles, and let the bed of coffee drain a little between pours. If the cup tastes sour, grind finer; if it tastes bitter, grind coarser.

values.title: Cold brew in five easy steps
values.excerpt: You need coarse coffee, cold water, a jar and a night in the fridge.
values.image_alt: Jars of cold brew steeping on a wooden shelf
values.author: The Ember team

children.text: Stir coarsely ground coffee into cold water in a clean jar, using one part coffee to five parts water. Cover it and leave it in the fridge for twelve to sixteen hours.
Strain through a paper filter, then dilute to taste with water or milk over ice. The concentrate keeps for a week in the fridge.

values.title: The spiced maple latte is back
values.excerpt: Our autumn favourite returns this week with real maple and a pinch of cinnamon.
values.image_alt: A spiced maple latte with a cinnamon stick
values.author: The Ember team

children.text: The spiced maple latte is on the menu again from this Monday, made with espresso, steamed milk, maple syrup and a pinch of cinnamon.
Order a medium one with any pastry before ten in the morning and the pastry is half price until the end of the month.

values.title: New seats by the window
values.excerpt: We have added a long window bench for slow mornings and laptop afternoons.
values.image_alt: New wooden window seats with cushions
values.author: The Ember team

children.text: A long bench now runs along the front window, with a socket under every second seat, so there is room to stay when the counter is busy.
Bring a book or a friend. The window seats are the quietest, and they catch the morning sun.

values.title: Home
values.intro_lead: Small-batch coffee, roasted in the shop and poured the way you like it.
values.story_left: We started with one small roaster and a counter by the window, roasting a little coffee every day so every cup is fresh.
values.story_right: The counter is longer now and the regulars know each other by name, but the coffee is still roasted slowly, by hand, a few steps from your table.
